author: ShadowPit
text:
Hello,

Firstly, I do not know where it will retrace to, nor do I create any expectations on where it will go. Secondly, that engulf you have marked off doesn't really tell you much, it also doesn't tell the same story on D1 charts, which suggests price has bounced from D1 demand. The area you have marked reversal, isn't very specific and thus I don't think it adds any value to your trading analysis. In regards to the fakeout you have marked, if you look on the daily its a perfect touch on a previous resistance area, so take from that what you will...Be careful with how you label things on your chart, you have labeled things on your chart which in combination give you conflicting bias on where to trade from and where to. Ok so onto what I think about the EURUSD:

EURUSD H4

EURUSD M15

If I were to short this chart the blue rectangle is where I would look for PA on the H4. ** I am interested in approach, because if price enters that area it will quite possibly engulf the FL with the green circle outline. If price creates demand when it breaks this FL I would be interested in seeing that demand engulfed before looking for short opportunities on the LTF. If I were to touch trade a short, I would be looking for price to approach the maroon area on the M15 chart. Ideally a compressed approach. Some things I would be cautious about if price reaches this area include what price looks like on the Weekly/Daily charts and if it is congruent with the LTF analysis, I would ask myself what this means for my trade targets and where I can logically take profit off or hold further. **Conversely if this area were to break I would look to find any long opportunities.

When you create some sort of a plan like the one above, you begin to anticipate where price will go (targets), and when your targets are correct more often than not, you begin to take trades in the opposite direction you're anticipating as price has not yet reached its target. So the other question you should be asking yourself is, how do I get in long, and where should I get out? It will ultimately come down to the other areas of your trading plan such as your profit objectives, risk management, how long you're willing to wait for price to reach your area, and how long you're willing to hold.

author: ShadowPit
text: I say target in the general sense. Price moves from supply to demand and visa versa. Price engulfs areas and then goes on to the next supply or demand. It's easier for me to use the word target when explaining an idea or concept as opposed to specific trades, as it is direction neutral.

As mentioned in the reply, on the daily chart I see price bouncing from demand at this level. If you were to call it an engulf on the H4 chart, then you have conflicting pieces of information which you need to resolve.

I find the HTFs are somewhat more reliable as creating your bias for trading direction. But when you apply your own analysis and find that you have timeframes which conflict with each other, you're better off finding a trade elsewhere or waiting for new PA until that conflict is resolved.

Edit: I am aware I haven't answered your questioned conclusively one way or the other and that is intentional. I am very mindful of what I say as it isn't up to me to tell you if this or that is an engulf, as I fear it would influence your decision making process creating unnecessary conflicts in your analysis as a result. So forgive me when I provide general guidance rather than anything specific. It's the thought process of analysing your trades that matters, and I will continue to provide advice that pushes & nudges to the ideas and concepts you might of missed and any advice which focuses on the overall picture to help fill in knowledge gaps.
